title: OneDrive for iOS and Android: annotate sensitivity-label protected PDFs
summary: The briefing passes: its availability, default and protected-PDF behaviour match the roadmap, and Microsoft Learn supports the existing PDF-support control and general annotation pricing. Independent searches found no feature-specific mobile annotation switch, minimum app version or separate licensing statement.

claims.claim: The OneDrive PDF features page describes general annotation and markup tools for mobile.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: The OneDrive PDF features page does not mention sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: Searched: 'OneDrive protected PDF annotation sensitivity label licensing price meter work school'; read the complete OneDrive PDF features page at learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/onedrive-pdf-features; it contains no sensitivity-label discussion.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The PDF-support control is at Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > Protect PDFs with Auto-labeling.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > Policies > Auto-labeling policies
Then, if you see a message Protect PDFs with Auto-labeling, select this banner

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -EnableSensitivityLabelforPDF $true turns on PDF support for sensitivity labels in SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote:
Alternatively, you can turn on PDF support by using PowerShell. Use the Set-SPOTenant cmdlet with the EnableSensitivityLabelforPDF parameter:
Set-SPOTenant -EnableSensitivityLabelforPDF $true

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: If the Protect PDFs with Auto-labeling banner is visible, selecting it confirms turning on PDF protection for files in SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: Then, if you see a message Protect PDFs with Auto-labeling, select this banner to confirm you want to turn on PDF protection for files in SharePoint and OneDrive.

claims.where: controls[0].governs and scope; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: The first control is the existing tenant setting for SharePoint and OneDrive PDF sensitivity-label support, not a mobile annotation switch.
claims.quote:
You can enable support for PDFs for the following scenarios:
- Applying a sensitivity label in Office for the web
- Uploading a labeled document, and then extracting and displaying that sensitivity label

claims.where: controls[0].note; Scope; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented whether the tenant PDF-support setting is a prerequisite for mobile annotation of protected PDFs.
claims.quote: Searched: 'OneDrive sensitivity label encrypted PDF annotations storage minimum app version iOS Android EnableSensitivityLabelforPDF prerequisite'; opened Purview SharePoint/OneDrive files and Office-app PDF support, and OneDrive PDF features; no mobile-annotation prerequisite is stated.

claims.where: controls[1].ui and api; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No feature-specific tenant UI switch or automation for disabling mobile annotation of protected PDFs is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'OneDrive mobile protected PDF annotation disable administrator PowerShell Set-SPOTenant policy iOS Android'; opened OneDrive PDF features and Purview SharePoint/OneDrive PDF support; results show general access controls, not a mobile annotation switch.

claims.quote: Assign permissions now, so that you can determine exactly which users get which permissions to content that has the label applied.

When you select Configure access control settings on the Access control page to create or edit a sensitivity label

claims.quote: Let users assign permissions when your users apply the label to content.

claims.claim: Enabling tenant PDF support can increase the number of files labelled by existing auto-labeling policies.
claims.quote: Enabling PDF support can increase the number of files that get automatically labeled by existing auto-labeling policies.

claims.claim: Microsoft states an absolute ceiling of 500,000 automatically labelled SharePoint and OneDrive files per tenant per day.
claims.quote: The absolute maximum throughput is 500,000 automatically labeled SharePoint and OneDrive files per tenant per day, in aggregate across all auto-labeling policies.

claims.quote: Searched: 'OneDrive protected PDF annotation sensitivity label licensing price meter work school'; read learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/onedrive-pdf-features in full; its pricing tables and subscription footnotes do not discuss labelled PDFs.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Sensitivity labels have Purview licensing requirements, and the service description says end users need appropriate licences for Information Protection functionality in their client applications.
claims.quote: Similarly, end users also need the appropriate licenses to use the functionality in their respective client applications.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost

claims.quote: Searched: 'OneDrive protected PDF annotation sensitivity label licensing price meter work school'; opened OneDrive PDF features, Purview service description and Purview PDF-support pages; general annotation pricing and label licensing are stated, but nothing specific to mobile protected-PDF annotation.

claims.where: Scope; Open questions
